argument_markdown:
## Source-backed inputs

ATT-0065, confirmed independently by REV-0108 and REV-0109, supplies the following load-bearing facts. CLM-0065-5 constructs the canonical filtration without globally splitting W and gives deg W_4=20 and deg W_5=16. CLM-0065-1 gives the locally free evaluation presentations and arbitrary base change. CLM-0065-3 gives coker(φ)≅coker(φ_5) from the filtered snake lemma. CLM-0065-2 and CLM-0065-4 identify the intrinsic Fitting ideal with a_N^*I_e scheme-theoretically over possibly nonreduced locally Noetherian bases. CLM-0065-7 through CLM-0065-9 give the conditional ambient comparison. SRC-0004 is used only through this confirmed dependency for the CE convention and degree formula.

## Proved step 1: ranks and the global maximal-minor identity

Since 20 and 16 exceed 2g−2=10, R^1π_*W_4=R^1π_*W_5=0. Riemann–Roch gives ranks 20−6+1=15 and 16−6+1=11. Because Γ is the disjoint union of six sections, each π_*(W_f|_Γ) has rank six. The filtration consequently gives ranks 26→12 for φ.

Also deg W_4(−Γ)=14>10, so R^1π_*W_4(−Γ)=0 and φ_4 is surjective. Applying the snake lemma to the two exact evaluation rows gives the canonical dependency-backed isomorphism coker(φ)≅coker(φ_5), without splitting W. Zeroth Fitting ideals depend only on the cokernel. Since φ and φ_5 are locally free presentations with target ranks 12 and 6,

Fit_0(coker φ)=I_12(φ)=Fit_0(coker φ_5)=I_6(φ_5).

This is a global identity of ideal sheaves, not the splitting-local block-minor product used unsuccessfully in ATT-0067. By CLM-0065-2 and CLM-0065-4, the common ideal is a_N^*I_e and commutes with arbitrary locally Noetherian base change.

## Proved step 2: the submaximal minors

Fix a geometric point b. From the evaluation sequence for W_{5,b} and H^1(W_{5,b})=0,

coker(φ_{5,b})≅H^1(C_b,W_{5,b}(−Γ_b)).

Serre duality identifies its dual with H^0(C_b,N_b), where N_b=ω_{C_b}⊗W_{5,b}^∨(Γ_b) has degree 10−16+6=0. A degree-zero line bundle on a smooth projective connected curve has either no section or is trivial with a one-dimensional section space. Hence dim coker(φ_b)=dim coker(φ_{5,b}) is either zero or one. Thus rank(φ_b) is always at least 11. Every geometric point therefore lies in an open on which some 11-by-11 minor is a unit, so I_11(φ)=O_B. This argument also shows that rank is exactly 11 on the failure locus and 12 off it.

## Proved step 3: geometric fibre and exact dimension formula

For an effective degree-six divisor Δ on C_b, the same degree-zero calculation gives rank drop exactly when H^0(ω⊗W_5^∨(Δ)) is nonzero, equivalently when ω⊗W_5^∨(Δ) is trivial, equivalently O(Δ)≅L_b=W_{5,b}⊗ω^{-1}. Thus the geometric rank-drop set is |L_b|. The full Abel–Jacobi fibre is the projective space of nonzero sections of L_b modulo scalars, so its dimension is h^0(L_b)−1.

Since deg L_b=16−10=6, Riemann–Roch gives χ(L_b)=1. With M_b=ω^2⊗W_{5,b}^∨=ω⊗L_b^{-1}, Serre duality gives h^1(L_b)=h^0(M_b), hence h^0(L_b)=1+h^0(M_b)≥1 and deg M_b=4.

If h^0(M_b)≤1, then h^0(L_b)≤2. If h^0(M_b)≥2, then h^1(M_b)=h^0(L_b)≥3, so M_b is special and Clifford gives h^0(M_b)−1≤deg(M_b)/2=2. Therefore h^0(M_b)≤3 in all cases, proving 1≤h^0(L_b)≤4.

For equality, h^0(M_b)=3 and |M_b| is a g^2_4. It has no base point, since removing a base point would give a degree-at-most-three line bundle with three sections, contradicting Clifford. The induced nondegenerate map C_b→P^2 has degree times image degree equal to four. It cannot be birational onto a plane quartic because the normalization of a plane quartic has genus at most three. Hence it is a double cover of a conic, so C_b is hyperelliptic and M_b is twice its g^1_2. Conversely, on a hyperelliptic curve h^0(2g^1_2)=3, so this condition gives h^0(L_b)=4.

## Proved step 4: reduced-support scope

The six-distinct-points locus is open in |L_b|. Ordering it is a finite étale S_6-torsor at stack level. Therefore its fibre is either empty or has the same dimension h^0(L_b)−1. Riemann–Roch proves nonemptiness only of the full |L_b| and does not prove this open is nonempty.

## Computational hypotheses and gaps

No finite experiment or computational hypothesis is used. The proof does not identify W_5 with ω^2(−D), does not infer any moduli-space image dimension from the fibre calculation, and makes no Hodge or Tate conclusion.

gap_markers.text: Nonemptiness of the reduced-support open and ordered Conf_6 incidence on every balanced geometric fibre remains open.
The theorem bounds h^0(L) but does not prove it is constant on the balanced locus.
No identification W_5≅ω^2(−D), and hence no rewrite L≅ω(−D), is asserted.
Balanced-base dimension, image dimension, numerical codimension, generic finiteness, components, stabilizers, closure, and local lci/Gysin structure in M_{6,6} remain unresolved.
Ambient comparison retains ATT-0065's separate hypothesis that q_*script-W is finite locally free and commutes with base change; fibrewise balancedness alone does not discharge that hypothesis.
The determinantal lemma does not establish purity, Tate type, vanishing, or the global target RED-0001.

summary: The global maximal-minor identity is obtained from the filtered cokernel isomorphism of dual-confirmed ATT-0065, repairing ATT-0067's splitting-open argument. A new submaximal-minor calculation proves I_11(φ)=O_B because the residual cokernel is dual to sections of a degree-zero line bundle and therefore has fibre dimension at most one. The geometric rank-drop fibre is |L|, with exact dimension h^0(L)−1 and the unconditional bound 0≤dim|L|≤3; the top value is characterized by the hyperelliptic Clifford-equality case. No W_5≅ω^2(-D), reduced-support nonemptiness, or image-codimension claim is used.

theorem_scope.base: locally Noetherian over a characteristic-zero field

theorem_statement: Theorem (filtered balanced CE rank computation at (g,n)=(6,6)). Let k be a characteristic-zero field, let B be a locally Noetherian k-scheme, let π:C→B be smooth proper with geometrically connected genus-six fibres, and let Γ be the union of six pairwise-disjoint sections. Assume the balanced tetragonal Casnati–Ekedahl data give the canonical filtration 0→W_4→W→W_5→0 with W_4 and W_5 invertible of fibre degrees 20 and 16. For the evaluation maps φ:π_*W→π_*(W|_Γ) and φ_f:π_*W_f→π_*(W_f|_Γ), put L=W_5⊗ω_{C/B}^{-1}, N=ω_{C/B}⊗W_5^∨(Γ), let a_N:B→Pic^0_{C/B} classify N, and let e be the identity section. Then π_*W_4, π_*W_5, π_*W, π_*(W_4|_Γ), π_*(W_5|_Γ), and π_*(W|_Γ) are locally free of ranks 15, 11, 26, 6, 6, and 12 respectively and have the stated arbitrary-base-change compatibility. Without any global splitting of W, coker(φ)≅coker(φ_5) canonically, and therefore Fit_0(coker φ)=I_12(φ)=I_6(φ_5)=a_N^*I_e. Moreover I_11(φ)=O_B: on every geometric fibre φ has rank 12 or 11 and never smaller. Thus the intrinsic ordered evaluation-failure scheme is scheme-theoretically the relative-triviality incidence for N, after arbitrary locally Noetherian base change and smooth-atlas descent. Under the additional ambient CE resolution and equation-bundle local-freeness/base-change hypotheses of ATT-0065, the ambient CE evaluation map has the same cokernel and failure scheme. For every geometric fibre C_b, the geometric rank-drop set among all effective degree-six divisors is the complete linear system |L_b|. If M_b=ω_{C_b}^{⊗2}⊗W_{5,b}^∨, then deg M_b=4 and h^0(L_b)=1+h^0(M_b), whence 1≤h^0(L_b)≤4 and dim|L_b|=h^0(L_b)−1∈{0,1,2,3}. Equality h^0(L_b)=4 holds exactly when C_b is hyperelliptic and M_b≅2g^1_2. The reduced-support ordered fibre is an open finite étale S_6-cover of the reduced-support open in |L_b|; it is either empty or has dimension h^0(L_b)−1.
